Seiko · ref. SPB383J1

PROSPEX 1968

Dive · 42–44.5mm · 200m, 300m · automatic

The Seiko Prospex 1968 is a family of professional dive watches known for their robust construction and high-frequency movements. Signature design cues include a distinctive angular case, a crown at the 4 o'clock position, and a high-contrast dial with large luminous markers.

The story

The family originated in 1968 with the release of the reference 6159-7000, which was Japan's first diver's watch with a high-beat 10-beat per second movement and 300m of water resistance. This model, and its successor the 6159-7001, were produced for a very short period, making them rare today. The design was revived in 2000 with the SBDX001 "Marinemaster 300," which became a cult classic and carried the torch for the 1968 design for over a decade. In recent years, Seiko has released a series of both faithful re-creations and modern re-interpretations, introducing new materials like ceramic bezels and sapphire crystals, and a wider range of movements, including the 6R series, to make the design accessible to a broader audience.
